title: The anthill at 300,000 frames -- re-shot on today's main
question: Which of these reads as an anthill that has stopped growing?
context_md:
**This replaces the card I posted an hour ago (20260912T115506982Z-6ae8e2) -- please judge this one.** That one's pictures were taken before the seed-cargo and round-trip fixes landed, and those changed the bed under it: the same seed went from 2,053 cells dug to 314. Same question, current code.

Both panes are frame 300,000 of two runs from an identical start, with one thing changed: **what an ant standing at its own door is asked before it digs.** One pane asks the old question, *how many ants are pressed against me*. The other asks *how much roofed room does this colony have, per ant*, so every chamber cut makes the next one less urgent.

**The loop works. It does not do what it was built for, and I would rather you knew both.** The colony answers the new question sensibly -- it digs hard while the burrow is bare, quietens at a few cells of room each, starts again as the brood outgrows them. But across **twelve beds run twice each** it left a *bigger* mound on nine of them, dug more on eight, and the spread between beds is absurd -- from a twenty-fifth of the mound to seventy times it. Nothing about it is reliable in either direction.

**And the premise it was built on is wrong.** I was told the old question is one an ant can never answer -- always 'yes, we are packed'. Counting what ants actually read at the door, 835,000 moments across twelve beds: **a third of the time there is nobody near the ant at all.** The old gate was never stuck. A mound that never regreens is not the door question; it is a colony outgrowing its rooms faster than it can cut them, which is the *number of ants* -- the lifespan work, not this.

**So I have shipped it off, which goes against your rule that new behaviours ship on.** On costs about 4% of a frame and builds more of the thing it was meant to reduce, and a default is the one form you cannot decline. It is one switch on the ANTS page. Tell me to put it back on and I will.
